line: Framework Laptop 13 (2025, AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series, DIY Edition)
config_name: Laptop 13 DIY — Ryzen AI 5 340, 16GB DDR5 (2x8GB), 1TB NVMe, 2.8K 120Hz matte display

specs.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI 5 340 (6-core/12-thread Zen 5/5c, up to 4.8GHz)
specs.ports: 4x user-swappable Expansion Card slots (USB-C/USB-A/HDMI/DP/Ethernet/microSD/storage; cards sold separately), 3.5mm
specs.os: None (DIY — bring your own; Windows or Linux)

battery.notes: 61Wh. Users report ~9-10.5h light use on Ryzen AI 300 boards; efficiency improved markedly over prior gens.

price.notes: Configurator component sum (2026-11-24): base $1,189 (was $1,289) + 16GB +$450 + 1TB SN7100 +$300. Excludes 4 expansion cards (~$15-36 ea) and OS license — real out-the-door ~$2,100+. DIY tiers listed low/out-of-stock at fetch time; prebuilt equivalents exist.

reviews.quote: Skip the Intel version for better performance. Pros: fast CPU with high performance-per-watt, readily available replacement parts, versatile USB-C expansion cards, FreeSync Premium support, easily serviceable. Cons: USB-C ports are not identical in terms of features, speakers and webcam are showing their age, lid and base susceptible to flexing, no OLED/P3/HDR.

praises: Socketed DDR5 SO-DIMMs and standard M.2 — RAM and storage upgraded by the owner in minutes, no soldering
Four swappable expansion-card ports let you choose exactly which ports you want (USB-A, HDMI, Ethernet, microSD)
Matte 3:2 2.8K 120Hz display is tall and sharp for code and documents
Every part is sold as a self-service spare with QR-coded repair guides; iFixit 10/10
First-class Linux support — official Ubuntu/Fedora guides, community-driven Arch/NixOS docs
complaints: Expansion cards and OS are extra-cost add-ons — sticker price understates real cost
1080p webcam is dated for 2026 and image quality is middling
Speakers are thin and quiet; users reach for headphones almost immediately
DIY edition requires assembling RAM/SSD and installing the OS yourself — friction for non-technical buyers
DIY tiers frequently out of stock; Framework's batch/inventory system forces waiting

design_philosophy: Framework's founding idea: a laptop that is a platform, not an appliance. Every component is standard, documented, and sold as a spare, and the mainboard is upgradeable across CPU generations, so this entry Ryzen AI 5 tier is an inexpensive entry into a chassis you can keep refreshing for years. The DIY edition shifts assembly to the buyer to cut cost and teach ownership.
standouts: Cheapest entry into a fully upgradeable, iFixit 10/10 laptop platform
Socketed RAM to 96GB and standard M.2 at under $2,000 CAD — unique in class
rating_notes: Pro score attached from NBC review of the Framework Laptop 13.5 Ryzen AI 9 (84%, gap-fill 2026-11-24). See SHARED-framework.md.
